In ''[[Red Dead Redemption 2]]'', the player character's condition can change overtime through the player's in-game actions. There are 4 categories: Weight, Temperature, Toxicity, and Wellbeing. ==Weight== The player character's weight is measured in a system of 0 (skinny) to 20 (overweight) points, and considered to be in perfect condition at 10 points. Weight has an effect on the physical appearance of both [[Arthur Morgan]] and [[John Marston]], and their [[Horse|horses]]. Body shape changes gradually with every weight point, but there are only three discrete face models (thin, average and chubby): PlayerWeightComparison.PNG Weights Comparison.jpg Arthur-Face_Models.gif
The weight of [[Red Dead Online protagonist]], whose body type is decided on character creation, has only very slight effect on his/her body shape, while the face doesn't change at all. As with [[Hair Growth|hair growth]], changes to weight do not happen in real time, but require loading screens to take effect, such as [[Fast Travel|fast traveling]] or [[sleeping]]. ===Effects of Weight=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align: center; width:100%;" ! style="background-color:#38090A" |Weight ! style="background-color:#38090A" |Effects |- | Overweight || 5.25% – 7.5% decrease in damage taken / increased stamina drain rate |- | Average || 0.75% – 4.5% decrease in damage taken / increased stamina drain rate |- | Perfect || 0%, no effects. All characters start at this weight. |- | Average || 0.75% – 4.5% increase in damage taken / decreased stamina drain rate |- | Underweight || 5.25% – 7.5% increase in damage taken / decreased stamina drain rate |} In addition, being at maximum or minimum weight will increase the drain rate of all cores by 25%. [[File:Weight table.png|alt=Detailed table of all weight effects|center|227x299px|Detailed weight table]] ===Managing Weight=== One weight point is lost every 12 in-game hours, which is approximately 24 real life minutesThe official game guide for Red Dead Redemption 2 erroneously states that one weight point is naturally lost every 24 in-game minutes, not 24 real life minutes. This would be 48 seconds in real time, meaning the player would go from max weight to minimum weight in only 16 minutes, or 2/3rds of an in-game day. (it is important to remember that the ratio is not always exactly 2 real life minutes/1 game hour, since the time flows faster during the night and fast-speed riding, among other factors). To gain 1 weight point, at least 10 in-game calories worth of food must be eaten. All consumables have their own caloric value: * No calories: Cigars/Cigarettes * 1 Calorie meals: All tonics, coffee, herbs and other foraged foods, opened alcohol, bread chunk, candies, and low quality meat * 3 Calorie meals: Alcohol from saloons and unopened bottles, most store-bought foods, medium quality meat, and Pearson's stew with no/low quality meat * 5 Calorie meals: Chocolate, Saloon meals, high quality meat, and Pearson's stew with medium/high quality meat * 10 Calorie meals: Big Game meat and Pearson's stew with Big Game meat For detailed caloric values of all provisions, see [[Provisions in Redemption 2]]. Ideally, to stay at constant weight, one should eat 10–19 calories worth of food every 12 in-game hours. A slight "crunch" sound is played after reaching 10 calories for the half-day. This can be easily achieved by eating 1 Big Game Meat, or 2 Chocolate/high quality meat (Prime Beef, Venison, Pork, or Exotic bird). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: left;" |'''Important note:'''
Skipped time (by [[sleeping]], [[Fast Travel|fast travel]] or waiting for shops to open) is '''not''' taken into account when the game calculates calories drain and intake rates. Only net time actually spend in the game counts as calories-draining hours. For example, if 24 hours have passed in the game, half of which were skipped in some way, the amount of calories consumed during that day needs to compensate only for 12 hours of natural weight loss and not for the whole day. One of the consequences of this is that advancing time with sleep or fast travel while not eating won't help in any way to '''lose''' weight, if there is such a need. On the other hand, skipping time will work very well for '''gaining''' weight – one should [[Consumables|consume]] at least 10 calories just before sleep or fast travel, and the weight will increase by one point after waking up or at the end of the trip. |} When the character is extremely underweight (specifically between +7.5% and +6% damage taken), it is not even necessary to eat before going to bed – even a shortest possible nap will add one point to the character's weight. Unfortunately, this doesn't work from the opposite end of the spectrum – even with maximal weight, sleeping on empty stomach won't make the character any less obese; the only way to lose weight is to actually spend time in the game while eating very little or nothing at all. Physical activity does not appear to have a significant effect on weight.
===Horse Weight=== Horses are also affected by the weight system, though to a lesser degree. Horse weight affects three things: * Their appearance will change slightly (though it can be very difficult to notice) gradually as they gain and lose weight. * The stable owner will almost always comment on the horse's current weight when entering the stables. * Overweight or underweight horses will receive a slight reduction in their top speed. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align: center; width:100%;" ! style="background-color:#38090A" |Weight ! style="background-color:#38090A" |Description |- | Malnourished || The horse is severely underweight. |- | Thin || The horse is underweight. |- | Fit || The horse is at a healthy weight. |- | Obese || The horse is severely overweight. |} [[File:HorseWeightComparison.PNG|center|700px]] ===Oversights=== *Arthur can get stuck with a chubby face no matter what his actual weight is (this usually happens in Chapter 4). There is no remedy for this bug on consoles. The only possible preventive measure is to make sure Arthur starts Chapter 4 weighing below +3.75% stamina drain rate (his weight must be adjusted before starting "[[A Short Walk in a Pretty Town]]"), though this can't guarantee the bug won't be triggered later. On PC there is a way to substitute the chubby head model with the average one with a [https://www.nexusmods.com/reddeadredemption2/mods/576 mod]. ==Temperature== Wearing improper clothing for the current climate can lead to the player becoming too hot or too cold, either of which incur a -900% health core drain rate. This can drain a full health core to zero in as little as 10 minutes. Different outfits can be saved on the player's horse via their wardrobe at [[Camps|camp]] or at a rented hotel/lodging area, and as such it is recommended to have at least one outfit for hot, temperate, and cold weather respectively saved on their horse when needed. For more information on clothing warmth values, see [[Weather in Redemption 2]]. ==Toxicity== The player character can become poisoned after being bitten by a [[Snake (RDR 2)|Snake]]. Like harsh weather conditions, this imposes a -900% health core drain rate. Poisoned can be cured by consuming [[Tonics in Redemption 2|Health Cures]] or one of various herbs (Ginseng, English mace, Milkweed, Vanilla flower, yarrow). ==Wellbeing== During the main story, Arthur [[A Fork in the Road|will become sick]] over the course of gameplay. This visibly changes his appearance and increases the drain rate of all cores by 20% (but first, the drain rate will increase by 5% until the diagnosis is made). All food will be less effective at refilling his cores while sick, as indicated by occasional heavy coughing after eating. ===Avoiding/Curing Sickness=== It is impossible to both continue the game's story and avoid becoming sick, as Arthur's sickness becomes a key plot point during [[Missions in Redemption 2#Chapter 6: Beaver Hollow|Chapter 6]]. However, symptoms and gameplay penalties do not appear until after completing Chapter 4. As such, it is recommended to take advantage of Arthur's wellbeing before starting Chapters 5 and 6, as the player will have to deal with faster core drain rates and lowered provision effectiveness for a long time afterwards. The only way to make the player character well again is by finishing the final story mission of Chapter 6, which will also complete the main story and begin the epilogue. ==References== ==Navigation== {{RDRII}} [[Category:Gameplay]]
